verdict.rationale: Sentry documents an official MCP server that connects external AI assistants for searching errors and analyzing performance. It also has a programmatic web API for managing and exporting data, backed by a published OpenAPI 3.0.3 schema covering the /api/0/ surface. Together these give an external agent a documented path into Sentry telemetry for debugging. However, the evidence never explicitly shows logs or metrics being queryable via the API or MCP; trace exploration is documented as a UI feature, and the API is v0 with beta endpoints subject to change. Missing for 10: explicit API/MCP querying of logs and metrics, documented trace-query endpoints, hands-on corroboration of an external agent debugging production.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an external agent query metrics, logs, and traces through documented APIs to debug production

citations.quote: Connects AI assistants to Sentry for searching errors, analyzing performance, triaging issues, reading documentation, and managing projects — all via the Model Context Protocol.
The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically. You can use the APIs to manage account-level resources, like organizations and teams, as well as manage and export data.
publishes the dereferenced OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for the "Sentry Public API"
